newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up on institutional support.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up on institutional support.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended up on Monday on institutional support buying in shares with a heavy index weighting including Pudong real estate shares, brokers said.
But trading volume was thin with most investors sidelined waiting for the listing of Jinan Qingqi Motorcycle Co's 230 million B shares on Tuesday, they said.
The B index rose 1.288 points or 1.53 percent to 85.219 points on volume of 12.933 million shares worth $8.648 million.
"The rebound of domestic A share market sparked a little speculative buying, which pushed the B index up, but trading remained dull with most investors cautious to follow," said one broker.
"Most investors are waiting for the listing of Jinan Qingqi and its performance will have great impact on the short-term market direction with its huge capitalization," another broker said.
Of 43 B shares, 39 traded, with 26 up, seven flat and six down.
The construction machinery maker Shanghai Jintai was the star on the basis of one speculative buy, soaring $0.012 or 9.23 percent to $0.142 on thin volume of 1,000 shares.
Shanghai Tyre & Rubber followed on a technical rebound, rising $0.040 or 8.33 percent to $0.520 on volume of 492,600 shares.
Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development was the most actively traded on institutional support, gaining $0.002 or 0.23 percent to $0.860 on volume of 1.7 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index continued to rebound, but investors seemed cautious amid the recent accelerated issue and listing of new shares, brokers said.
The index rose 18.210 points or 1.40 percent to 1,317.132 on volume of 457.9 million shares worth 6.2 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index went up 54.396 points or 1.42 percent to 3,879.783 points.

Shanghai Jiabao Industry and Commerce was the biggest gainer on institutional speculative buying, surging 1.13 yuan or 10.01 percent to 12.41 yuan on volume of 2.5 million shares. -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
